description.narrative:
Green Jobs Proof Lab is a youth-led (18–35) innovation sprint in Matola/Boane,Mozambique, turning climate action into real livelihoods for marginalised young people, especially young women. We will recruit 30 Youth Proof Fellows and run two 8-week sprints where teams test and improve two low-cost green micro-services (repair/reuse and waste-to-value). The innovation is our Proof-to-Adoption System: each team produces a “Proof Pack” with verified outputs, income/placement results, cost per outcome, and a simple replicationguide. We use Proof Packs to secure Adoption Deals with TVET partners,municipalities and employers (micro-contracts, internships and/or curriculum add-ons).We publish a short toolkit and share learning through YAL’s Africa–Europe community and Link <(>&<)> Learn so other youth organisations can replicate the model.
Goal: enable marginalised youth (18–35), especially young women, to access green income opportunities while generating proof that partners can adopt. Objectives: (1) recruit and coach 30 Youth Proof Fellows; (2) test and improve 2 green micro-services through two sprints; (3) secure at least 3 Adoption Deals with TVET, municipal and employer partners.
Activities: co-design + partner pledges; Sprint 1 test; Sprint 2 improve <(>&<)> expand; DemoDays; placements/micro-contracts; peer mentoring + safe participation supports;toolkit + YAL peer learning.

participating-org.narrative:
AADIS is a youth-led, non-profit organisation in Mozambique that empowers young people, especially young women and marginalised youth, to lead their own development. We design and deliver practical programmes that combine skills, employability pathways, inclusion, protection/safeguarding, and evidence-based learning. Our approach is strongly community-rooted and partnership-driven, working with public institutions, private companies, training providers, and local actors to improve youth outcomes and promote sustainable, inclusive development.
AADIS is youth-led by definition: young people aged 18–35 represent 100% of the organisation’s governance andhold primary decision-making power over organisational direction, strategy, and programmes. The organisation’s core functions (programme design and delivery, partnerships/outreach, monitoring and learning, community engagement, and operations) are also implemented primarily by youth aged 18–35 (>80%). Young people do not only “participate”; they lead planning, implementation, and learning. Where we engage external experts, they serve only as non-voting technical advisors and do not hold decision-making authority. Proof isprovided through the uploaded organogram and age list for leadership, governance, and key staff roles.
